title: Wind, Solar and Other Renewable Generation (Daily, CEA)
description: Daily all-India generation from renewable energy sources (wind, solar, and other RES such as biomass, bagasse and small hydro) from CEA's Daily Renewable Generation Report, in million units (MU) net. Large hydro is not part of this series (it is in the daily generation-by-source indicator). Solar and wind output explains much of the daily swing in coal generation, so this series is needed to read daily power demand correctly.
source: Central Electricity Authority (Renewable Project Monitoring Division), Daily Renewable Generation Report

qna.question: What does this measure?
qna.answer: Energy generated on the day by grid-connected wind, solar and other renewable plants, all India, in million units (MU) net. It is the 'All India' row of CEA's daily renewable report, which also splits it by state and region.^Large hydro, nuclear and thermal are in the daily generation-by-source indicator.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Solar output is highly seasonal (lowest in the monsoon, highest in spring) and wind peaks in the south-west monsoon, so use the YoY view. Strong YoY growth is mostly capacity additions, not demand; to read demand, add this series to the daily generation series (total generation = both).^A rise in renewables with flat coal output means falling reliance on coal, not weak demand.

qna.question: Definitions, revisions and caveats
qna.answer: Data are reported by state load dispatch centres and are provisional; they cover only the renewable capacity that reports to CEA (not rooftop/behind-the-meter solar). The monthly series uses the report's cumulative month figure on the last day of the month.^The daily file archive starts on 30 June 2024; missing days are left blank. The source host is gen-re.cea.gov.in (a CEA host that is separate from cea.nic.in).
